title: How to Build Quality Gates into Agentic Coding Workflows — Nnenna Ndukwe, Qodo AI
talk_summary: A Qodo DevRel lead demos a structured agentic coding workflow: repo-local rules/skills/AGENTS.md, a detailed two-tier planning template, deterministic local gates (ruff, pyright, bandit, pytest, conventional commits), then PR review whose findings are auto-remediated by an agent skill and re-verified. The transferable core is codifying standards once and reusing them as context at planning, implementation, and review, plus severity-tiered rules that deterministically block merges.

takeaways.technique: Repo-local rules + skills as shared context across phases
takeaways.what_they_do: Standards live in a rules/ and skills/ directory plus AGENTS.md; the agent is asked to select which rule IDs are relevant to the task and explain why, and the same rules are ingested by the PR reviewer.

A high-level plan (behavior change, applicable rules, skills, tests, gates) plus an execution plan capturing starting branch, verification commands, skill handoff, step list, and definition-of-done/deferrals.
Run linters, static analysis, type checks, tests, and conventional-commit checks locally as a verification command before opening a PR, combined with AI review rather than replacing it.
takeaways.evidence_quote: I am a huge believer in combining deterministic tools with uh AI

takeaways.technique: Severity-tiered rules with deterministic merge blocking
takeaways.what_they_do: Rules are categorized (correctness, security, maintainability, etc.) and assigned severity; high/action-required findings block merge until fixed and re-verified.
takeaways.evidence_quote: There are some rules that are strong enough to where you want to block a merge. There are others that are just like it's good practice

takeaways.technique: PR-resolver skill that fixes reviewer findings then re-verifies
takeaways.what_they_do: An agent skill pulls the reviewer's findings from the PR, autofixes or defers each, reruns the verification command, commits conventionally, and posts a fix summary back to the PR.
takeaways.evidence_quote: it's pulled down all of the issues that COD has already identified from critical to high ... then it's going to run verification

takeaways.technique: Skill evaluation tooling (Tessl) for skill value/security
takeaways.what_they_do: A third-party tool evaluates whether a skill is effective and free of security concerns, since the review platform only ingests skills without judging them.
takeaways.evidence_quote: it will tell you are there any security concerns with this skill or is this actually as effective as you expect it to be
